To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) parental health, especially that of the wife, is an important determinant of child health; 2) the prices of food and non-food items have a significant impact on child health, but the price of food items consumed mostly by children is more important than other prices; 3) the number of children in the family is an important determinant; and 4) genetic inheritance has an important influence on child health.

the health of children is negatively related to the prices of food consumed by them; the health of children of parents with better health is better; the health of older children is better; the number of siblings of wives is negatively related to children health; altitude negatively affects the health; and the health of children and that of their parents are highly correlated.
child health is determined by the health of parents, the age and sex of the child, and by the prices of food that are mostly consumed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determinants of the health of children in rural Ethiopia, and the role played by the genetic endowments, parental and child health.

three main issues: (a) the determinants of the health of children, (b) the relationship between the health of parents and children and (c) the role of genetic inheritance in the relationship between parents’ and children’s health.
the determinants of long-term child health in Ethiopia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the health of children is determined by the health of their parents, their own age, gender, birth order, the age and gender of their mother, the number of children in the household, the altitude and the prices of food that are mostly consumed.
the health of children is mainly determined by the height of the parents and that of the wife in particular.
children’s health is determined mainly by genetic endowments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
child health in rural areas is mainly influenced by the height of the parents and by the prices of food consumed by children.
the health of children is mainly affected by genetic endowments, parental health, and the price of food.
the height of the mother has a significant and positive impact on child health in rural areas of Ethiopia, and that the health of the child is not significantly affected by the health of the father.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, while the health status of children in rural Ethiopia is strongly influenced by genetic inheritance, it is also affected by the nutritional status of their mothers, and to some extent, by that of fathers.
the role of genetic inheritance in determining child health is more important than previously believed.
genetic endowments, which are largely unobservable and unmeasured, play a significant role in determining child health.
